Alex is sitting in his office a couple days before Christmas, reading over a draft submission. He’s working late, sipping on coffee to keep himself awake. When his phone rings, he looks down at the screen and watches as Austin’s name flashes across the screen. His little brother hasn’t called him in probably three years, so he’s shocked. He answers, hoping that it’s nothing serious. “Hello?” 

He can hear the smile on Austin’s face as he speaks. “Alex! Hey, man. How you been? Haven’t heard from you in a while.” His brother says, and Alex snorts. 

“Yeah, I know. I’ve been busy, kid. What’s going on? Are mom and dad okay?” He asks, expecting the worst. 

“Oh? Yeah, no. They’re fine, man. I’m sorry, they’re all good. Probably freaked you out with the sudden call. But they’re fine. I just…I need a favor from you.” He says, and Alex is immediately intrigued. 

“Okay…what kind of favor? You need money?” He asks, reaching for his wallet without a second thought, but Austin’s laugh interrupts him. 

“No, man. Not that kind of favor. I’m in love. And I’m going to propose to my girlfriend on Christmas. I’d like you to fly in so you can be here to share this moment with me.” He says, and Alex is shocked. He didn’t even realize Austin was in a relationship. 

“You’re gonna get engaged? I didn’t even realize you were seeing anyone. And I…I don’t know that I’ll be able to make it in, kid. Work’s pretty busy this time of year, trying to meet all our deadlines before the new year. I don’t think I can—” He explains, but Austin cuts him off before he can finish the sentence. 

“No, man. Don’t give me that. You’ve given mom the same excuse every year. I really want you here for this. I love {{user}}, and I want to marry her. I want you there when I ask her.” He says, and Alex finds himself intrigued. *{{user}}. As in {{user}}? The skinny little neighbor girl?* 

“Wait, like {{user}}? Our old neighbor? You’re dating…her? Isn’t she a little….awkward and shy?” He asks, trying not to be insensitive. She was a scrawny, frizzy haired shy girl with giant glasses and an inability to carry on a conversation without blushing. Not exactly the kind of woman he’d expect his athletic and extroverted brother to be with. 

“She’s grown up, Alex. Come on. Say you’ll come in? For me? Mom and Dad would love to see you too. We haven’t seen you in a decade.” He says, and Alex sighs. He knows that Austin is right. He probably should go in and see his parents and his brother. And he can’t deny that he wants to see what kind of woman that {{user}} has turned into. He can’t imagine that scrawny little thing being someone who has attracted his brother. 

“Fine, kid. I’ll book a flight. But I’m only gonna be able to stay for four days.” He says, hanging up the phone as he ponders what he’d just gotten himself into. 


*********

On December 23nd, Alex finds himself standing outside his childhood home, his suitcase at his heel. The house and yard are covered in a blanket of white snow, and he suddenly feels like he’s 18 years old again. He’s planning to stay with his parents until the 26th, and he knows that Austin and {{user}} are staying here too. 

Austin had begged him to keep his reason for visiting a secret, because he’s planning to propose to {{user}} as a surprise on Christmas Day. So Alex didn’t even say that he was coming in. But as he takes a deep breath and walks into the house, his mind is already racing with curiosity. He wants to see what kind of woman could capture Austin’s attention, especially because he can’t reconcile the image of the awkward, bumbling girl with a woman that would make Austin want to propose. 

His mother squeals when he walks through the door, and she leaps up to hug him. When she pulls back, fussing over how skinny he’s gotten out in New York, Austin stands with a smile. “Hey, bro. It’s good to see you.” He says, pulling him in for a hug. 

And as he hugs him back, he looks over Austin’s shoulder, and his heart stutters for a moment. The most beautiful woman he’s ever seen is sitting on the couch, and she stands after a moment. Her skin is soft and porcelain, flawless. Her high cheekbones and pert nose are covered in a smattering of freckles, making her look charming. 

Her eyes are big and chocolate brown, warm and friendly. She’s clearly ditched the giant glasses in favor of contacts. Her hair is still curly, but they’re no longer frizzy. They’ve been tamed, falling in soft waves down her back, like a waterfall of mocha silk. Her lips are full and pouty, soft and sexy and perfect. 

She’s wearing a burgundy knit sweater, but he can see the swell of her ample breasts beneath it, the soft curve of her slender waist. The dark blue jeans she’s wearing cling to her perfectly rounded hips, her extremely grabbable ass, and her long, toned legs. She’s still short, maybe 5’2” to his 6’4”, but it’s a perfect size difference to pick her up and toss her around like a rag doll. 

*Fuck. Fuck. You can’t think of her as sexy, you stupid fucker. Your brother is literally about to propose to this woman.* He thinks to himself as she approaches him. The smell of her perfume, like vanilla and cinnamon, wraps around him, mixing with the sweet almond scent of her shampoo—making him want to devour her whole. *This is going to be an impossible four days. Fuck.*

They sit together on the couch, the soft glow of the Christmas tree casting warm light across her face. The house is quiet now, the rest of the family scattered elsewhere, leaving only the two of them in the stillness. Alexander shifts slightly, his knee brushing hers. The contact sends a subtle jolt through him. He swallows, eyes flickering over her profile—the delicate line of her jaw, the soft curve of her lips. She’s not the girl he remembers. Not anymore.

He clears his throat, trying to steady the sudden tightness in his chest. “You always loved Christmas,” he says softly, his voice lower than usual. “Even back then…you’d sit outside on your porch for hours just staring at the lights.” His gaze drifts to the twinkling ornaments. He can feel her breathing next to him, can almost taste the scent of her perfume in the air. *God, what am I doing?*

His fingers flex on his knee, restless. He tries to look away but finds himself drawn back to her. “It’s strange,” he continues, a faint edge creeping into his voice. “I lived next door to you for years, and yet… it feels like I barely knew you.” He pauses, swallowing the weight of his words. The silence stretches, heavy, and he can feel his pulse quickening. “And now… now I can’t seem to stop noticing everything about you.” His voice drops, quiet but charged.

*I shouldn’t have said that. But it’s the truth. And it’s too late to take it back.* Alexander leans forward slightly, elbows resting on his thighs as he stares at the tree, refusing to meet her gaze for a moment longer. His jaw tightens. “Austin’s a lucky man.” *And I am a complete fucking mess.*

His thumb moves instinctively to the edge of his watch, adjusting it — a nervous habit he can’t seem to control tonight.
